To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have shown that the spatial distribution of heating in the corona can be di erent in the case of AC and DC heating mechanisms and that this di erence can be observed in emission line profiles.
the spatial distribution of energy input in the corona for AC and DC heating is significantly different and that this leads to a di erent spatial distribution of the emission in the corona.

the di erence of the spatial distribution of energy input for parameterizations of di erent heating mechanisms can be used to distinguish these mechanisms and that the spatially more homogeneous heating in an AC model leads to higher coronals temperatures and a more extensive transition region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spatial distribution of heating in the corona and its consequences.
the spatial distribution of energy input in parameterisations of coronal heating mechanisms and the resulting coronal emissions.
parameterisations of coronal heating.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the coronal heating mechanism is not yet determined by observations.

a homogeneous distribution of the heat along a loop, as expected from an AC mechanism, is a good indicator of Alfven waves, while a strong drop in the heat input towards its top is a good indicator for a DC mechanism.
the spatial distribution of coronal heating is an important observable to constrain the coronal heating mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we need to understand the spatial distribution of coronal heating better before drawing final conclusions on the underlying physical mechanism.
we need to understand the heating mechanisms better to be able to use them to interpret observations of the corona.
, in general, the energy input is more concentrated towards the foot points of field lines in the case of DC heating, while the coronal emission is more concentrated for the case of AC heating.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spatial distribution of heating has a large impact on the coronal temperature structure and thus on the resulting emission.
the spatial distribution of heating and emission is not only a function of the heating rate but also of its temporal evolution.
the spatial distribution of coronal heating is not a simple function of the magnetic field strength.
